structure.title: How parking fees work
items: Base fee: a flat fee for the first block of time (e.g. 30 minutes).
Extra fee: charged per unit (e.g. 5 or 10 minutes) after the base time. Even one minute over adds a full unit.
Grace period: leave within this time (e.g. 10 minutes) and pay nothing.
Free time: validation from marts, hospitals, etc. is subtracted from your parking time first.
Daily max: each 24 hours from entry never costs more than this. Two days means up to twice the cap.
Discounts: compact/low-emission and disabled discounts apply as a percentage of the final fee.

tips.title: Ways to save
items: Watch the 'next increase' notice and leave just before the next unit starts.
Seoul public parking has three grades charging 500/250/150 KRW per 5 minutes (on-street; grade-1 off-street lots charge 400 KRW). Grade 3 is the cheapest.
Mart and department store free time depends on how much you spend — check the threshold and keep your receipt.
For long stays, lots with a daily max win. Use the comparison to see when they overtake each other.
If you park somewhere often, compare a monthly pass with your expected monthly fee.

whatIs.title: What is the Parking Fee Calculator?
whatIs.description: The Parking Fee Calculator computes the total parking cost by taking into account entry and exit times, base rates, free parking periods, per-unit additional fees, and daily maximum caps. It accurately simulates real parking lot pricing structures, making it useful for budgeting parking expenses or creating parking rate guides.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the parking start and end times.
2. Set the base rate and free parking period (e.g., 30 minutes free).
3. Enter the additional rate per time unit (e.g., ₩500 per 10 minutes).
4. If there is a daily maximum, enter that value and review the calculated result.

items.q: Can it handle overnight or multi-day parking?
items.a: Yes. Choose 'By entry/exit time' and pick the next day (or later) as the exit date. The daily max is applied separately for each 24 hours from entry.

items.q: How is the daily max applied?
items.a: This calculator splits the fee into 24-hour blocks starting at entry and caps each block at the daily max. Some lots settle at midnight instead, so check the posted rules.

items.q: In what order are free time and discounts applied?
items.a: Free time (including purchase-based free time) is subtracted first, the daily max is applied to the remaining fee, and the discount percentage is applied last. Amounts under 10 KRW are dropped.
It is built for hourly fees. To see if a pass pays off, enter your expected monthly parking time and compare the result with the pass price.
